project.max_plates.measured_on: one slicer version: it crashed opening a project with 37 plates
project.max_plates.description: most plates one .3mf project may hold

rules.title: Every STL in an STL folder has a stamp
rules.statement: Every STL in a registered STL folder was written by gate.py export and has a valid stamp.
rules.why: STLs were written by three exporters with three part tables; nothing said which of them had been checked.
fix_order: Export the part through the gate (gate.py export) and place the new STL.
An STL made by code: gate.py export --generated.

rules.title: Every STL is placed in a project
rules.statement: Every STL of a registered STL folder matches an object of at least one registered .3mf project.
rules.why: A mesh swap silently skipped an STL that matched no object: the project kept the old geometry.
fix_order: Add the part to a plate.
Remove an STL that is no longer a part.

rules.title: Every object is on a plate
rules.statement: Every object of a registered .3mf project sits on a plate.
rules.why: A plate was deleted in the slicer; its object stayed in the project off the plates and every later mesh swap skipped it.
fix_order: Give the object a plate again.
Remove the object if the part is gone.

rules.title: A switched-off object is a decision
rules.statement: An object of a registered .3mf project that is not printable is listed: it is not sliced and not checked by any slice.
rules.why: Objects switched off in the slicer were skipped by the support check and went unnoticed.
fix_order: Switch the object on.
Left off on purpose: owner waiver naming the object.

rules.title: Every mesh in a project has a stamp
rules.statement: Every mesh of a registered .3mf project is the geometry of a valid stamp.
rules.why: Nothing tied a mesh on a plate to a checked export: unchecked geometry was printed.
fix_order: Export the part through the gate (gate.py export) and place the new STL.

rules.title: No project holds an older geometry than its STL
rules.statement: The mesh of every object equals the current stamped STL of its part.
rules.why: A project still held a part without a pocket that had been added to the model and exported the day before.
fix_order: Swap the mesh from the stamped STL.

rules.title: Build table and project agree
rules.statement: The plates and objects of a project equal its build table, when the table is a pure literal.
rules.why: A build script still listed a part on a plate that had been moved in the saved project.
fix_order: Update the build table to the saved project, or rebuild the project from the table: ask the owner which one is right.

rules.title: A part is judged for the nozzle it is printed with
rules.statement: The nozzle and line width of a .3mf project equal its declared target, and every stamp of its meshes was judged for that target.
rules.why: A toothed part was right in CAD and unprintable on the wider nozzle of the project it was placed in.
fix_order: Export the part for the target of this project.
Move the part to the project with the right nozzle.
The declared target is wrong: the owner corrects gate/project.json.

rules.title: The project prints with the settings its fits were measured under
rules.statement: The declared target of a .3mf project (gate/project.json) says the slicer settings every fit was measured under: {target.fit_settings}. The global value of each one in the project file, and every per-object override, equals the declared value; so does the value every object prints with for each print setting of the target's "print" block (enable_support, support_type, support_remove_small_overhang, wall_sequence). A difference is put back in the project, or the owner changes the declared target: then every fit measured under the old value is open again.
rules.why: The X-Y hole compensation of a project went from 0.125 to 0 during a tool write, and nothing compared it. Every hole of every part printed from that project since was about 0.25 mm smaller than its fit assumed, and a bought magnet did not go in.
fix_order: Put the setting back in the project: python3 bambulab/tools/set_3mf_setting.py for an object, bambu3mf.set_project for the global value.
A setting that was changed on purpose: the owner changes the declared target in gate/project.json. Fits measured under the old value are D again until they are printed.
A setting the declared target does not say yet: the owner adds it to "targets" in gate/project.json.

rules.title: A tool write does not change a fit setting unasked
rules.statement: Every save of a .3mf through the tools compares the fit settings ({target.fit_settings}) of the archive about to be written with the file on disk, the global values and the per-object overrides. A changed setting that the caller did not name is refused in enforce mode and is one loud line in observe mode. A writer cannot say "settings kept": the tool compares them.
rules.why: A tool write changed the X-Y hole compensation of a project from 0.125 to 0. Its commit message said the settings were kept. Nobody had compared them.
fix_order: A change that was not meant: find what replaced the settings (a template laid over the project, a rebuild) and write the project from its saved state.
A change that is meant: make it with bambu3mf.set_project, set_settings or set_3mf_setting.py, which name the setting to the guard, or call bambu3mf.note_setting(key, value) before the save.
Then the owner changes the declared target in gate/project.json, or project.settings_match fails.
rules.note: Enforced inside bambu3mf.save() by the guard (gate_guard.check). gate.py verify judges no write: the rule passes there.

rules.title: A project is never written while the slicer has it open
rules.statement: A project file is never written while the slicer has it open. Unsaved changes in the slicer stop the edit and go to the owner. The slicer is opened again only if it was running before. One project is open at a time.
rules.why: A script that rewrote an open project reset the owner's filament choice; rebuilds kept undoing his manual edits.
fix_order: Run the writer through the wrapper that checks the slicer is closed.
The slicer is open with unsaved changes: stop and ask the owner.

rules.title: A build syncs into the saved project
rules.statement: A later build syncs into the saved project and keeps what the owner changed by hand: filaments, positions, the prime tower. It never rebuilds from a template. A conflict stops the write and is listed. A setting made by hand goes into the build table.
rules.why: Rebuilds undid manual moves and material choices several times.

rules.title: A mesh swap keeps the bed face and the pose
rules.statement: A mesh swap keeps the part on its recorded bed face and in its exact pose, refuses an STL that is still in the CAD frame, and decides "unchanged" by comparing vertices, not counts or volumes. A part that prints flipped keeps its bounding box under a raw swap: look at the bed face after the swap, not only at the box.
rules.why: Six parts stood on the wrong face after a swap from raw STLs. Three times a project silently kept an old mesh after the model had changed.
rules.note: The mesh swap of the plugin refuses a box with swapped axes; a flipped part and a near-cubic part are not refused.

rules.title: Every changed plate is sliced before it is called ready
rules.statement: Every built or changed plate is sliced headless before the owner is told it is ready. No mesh has open edges. Every object sits on the bed, inside it, off the keep-out areas and apart from its neighbours. A passing headless slice does not prove that the slicer window opens the file.
rules.why: Two parts ended 5 and 8 mm inside the bed.

rules.title: Plates are named, never empty, and printed parts stay
rules.statement: Every plate has a name that says its status and its contents, and is never empty. A part printed N times is one object with the count in the plate name. A printed part stays in the project and its plate says so; a superseded part leaves it. One project holds one nozzle and at most {project.max_plates} plates. One layer height per plate.
rules.why: A part was taken out of the project because it was "already printed"; the owner put it back. A superseded part sat on a production plate until someone noticed.

rules.title: A support blocker is placed again when its hole moves
rules.statement: A mesh swap keeps support blockers where they were. That is right only while the change does not touch what they cover. After a hole, a tunnel or a window moved, each blocker of that object is placed again and the plate is sliced.
rules.why: Nothing checks a blocker after its hole has moved; supports inside holes were found on printed parts.

rules.title: Blockers are modifier parts, and the file keeps its format
rules.statement: A support blocker is a modifier part with the right part id, or it prints solid. Meshes start at z = 0. Names avoid characters the slicer refuses. Per-filament arrays keep their stride. A pause for inserts or nuts is a multiple of the layer height.
rules.why: A base was printed with a solid slab over its screw pockets: the blockers had been written as normal parts.
rules.note: Kept by the tests of the .3mf writers in the plugin.
